title: Crypto misuse: GCM sess_init error paths missing memzero_explicit
description:
wolfssl_aes_gcm_sess_init has three error-unwind paths that call kfree(ctx) without first calling memzero_explicit(ctx, sizeof(*ctx)):

1. wc_AesInit failure (line 112-114): ctx->op is set; no key material yet. Low severity but inconsistent with the pattern.

2. wc_AesGcmSetKey failure (line 118-121): wc_AesFree is called but memzero_explicit is missing. After wc_AesGcmSetKey ran, ctx->aes holds partial or full AES key schedule in the kernel-expanded key tables. Freeing ctx without memzero_explicit leaves key schedule bits in freed memory — FIPS 140-3 zeroization violation.

3. wc_InitRng_ex failure (line 124-128): wc_AesFree is called but memzero_explicit is missing. At this point wc_AesGcmSetKey succeeded, so ctx->aes holds the fully-expanded AES-GCM key schedule. Freeing without memzero_explicit is a FIPS 140-3 zeroization failure.

Trigger: any failure of wc_InitRng_ex during sess_init (e.g. entropy source unavailable) leaves AES key schedule material in freed heap.

Compare: wolfssl_aes_cbc_sess_init correctly calls memzero_explicit(ctx, sizeof(*ctx)) on all error paths (lines 103, 115, 124).

Fix: add memzero_explicit(ctx, sizeof(*ctx)) before kfree(ctx) on all three GCM error paths, matching the CBC pattern.
close_reason: fixed: added goto err_free_ctx with memzero_explicit(ctx, sizeof(*ctx)) before kfree on all error paths in wolfssl_aes_gcm_sess_init
